text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Itsekiri tribe walks out of judicial commission investigating prolonged ethnic clashes in oil town of Warri over relocation of the local council headquarters.
- Hope rises on end to fuel shortage as materials for maintenance of Warri oil refinery which had been seized by customs department are released.
- Widespread arrest of soldiers and politicians in Sierra Leone over allegation of plotting counter coup to topple soldiers who seized power there in May.
- Customs department plans sacking of 3,000 officers in an operation to rid itself of corruption, official sources say.
- Guiness Nigeria spends 596.5 million naira in restructuring the firm, including paying off 921 staff made redundant as a result, company sources say.

- Capital allocations for first and second quarters of this year are still being withheld by the federal government because it wants to consolidate on the gains of reforms of the last two years, says national planning minister Ayo Ogunlade.
- At least 18 people died in new clashes on Sunday between Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes in oil town of Warri, witnesses said.
- Nigeria's private sector anticipates that the nation's naira currency will further depreciate despite assuarances by the finance minister that it will not be devalued.
- Slowdown in Nigeria's economy worries experts.
- Nigeria's external reserves rise to $5.9 billion by end of March 1997 from $4.086 billion at the end of 1996.
